conflicts.prohibit: The pictures are only stored locally in the app and are not accessed or used by GN Hearing nor shared with any third parties.
conflicts.situation: A user takes pictures of their face and hearing aids in a Beltone app feature that uses facial recognition for fitting.
conflicts.reason: The CCPA notice lists biometric information as collected, while the app section says facial pictures stay on the device; the policy names no other biometric source or says which statement governs.

conflicts.permit: We may share certain marketing metrics including Personal Information, anonymous (de-identified) information, and statistical information derived from your use of the Services, with our business partners for any purpose, including to help improve our services and determine the effectiveness of certain advertising campaigns.
conflicts.prohibit: they will only use your contact data and other Personal Information to carry out their specific business obligations to Everseat
conflicts.situation: Everseat shares marketing metrics containing a user's Personal Information with a business partner that also performs hosting or billing services for Everseat.
conflicts.reason: Both statements refer to business partners without distinguishing groups. One permits sharing Personal Information for any purpose, the other limits partners' use to obligations to Everseat, and no precedence is stated.

conflicts.permit: we will ensure consent is obtained from parents for the collection, use and sharing of their children's personal information
conflicts.prohibit: MobiVio Services are intended for general audiences and do not knowingly collect any personal information from children.
conflicts.situation: A user identifies as under 13 in a MobiVio service that requests age, and a parent gives consent, so MobiVio collects the child's personal information.
conflicts.reason: The first statement denies any knowing collection from children without exception, while the second describes knowing collection from self-identified under-13 users with parental consent. Neither statement references the other as an exception.

conflicts.permit: with our trusted services providers who work on our behalf, do not have an independent use of the information we disclose to them, and have agreed to adhere to the rules set forth in this privacy statement.
conflicts.prohibit: Only aggregated, anonymized data is periodically transmitted to external services to help us improve the Application and our service.
conflicts.situation: Battle Creek Games sends a user's registration data or device ID to a trusted service provider that helps improve the Application.
conflicts.reason: One statement limits transmissions to external services to aggregated, anonymized data, while the disclosure list permits sending identifiable User Provided and Automatically Collected Information to service providers. The policy does not say which governs.

conflicts.permit: These partners may access your data and operate under their own privacy policies.
conflicts.prohibit: These partners process your data only at and according to our instructions to provide the Service, such as hosting, player support, advertising, analytics and fraud prevention.
conflicts.situation: An advertising or analytics partner such as Google or Unity receives player data from the GlobalFun Service and uses it.
conflicts.reason: Partners performing advertising and analytics are said to act only on GlobalFun's instructions, yet advertising partners operate under their own policies. The policy does not say how a partner in both groups is treated.

conflicts.permit: the Personal data that users provide us will be shared to Drivers for the latter to carry out and complete Transport
conflicts.prohibit: We do not distribute, sell, share or disclose personal data to third parties except under the following limited circumstances
conflicts.situation: A user's address and phone number are shared with the Driver assigned to the user's delivery request.
conflicts.reason: The exception list covers trusted partners and legal orders but not Drivers. The policy does not say whether Drivers, who are separate users providing Transport, count as third parties.
